messages:
Emma Hart: Customer @acme-app opened a ticket — they started getting intermittent 429 spikes after increasing context to ~64k tokens and switching to rwd-3-large. They report ~1.6k requests/minute and ~55k tokens/minute, mostly short chat messages but with large prepended system context. Body of error: "error: rate_limit_exceeded, model_rpm". Can SRE confirm whether this looks like model-specific RPM/TPM, or a global quota?

Raj Patel: Thanks Emma — can you paste the raw response headers and a minimal repro curl? Also which API key (prod/dev) and region?

Emma Hart: Pasting sanitized headers from customer's failing call: 
```
HTTP/1.1 429 Too Many Requests
Date: Mon, 09 Nov 2026 14:02:13 GMT
x-rw-rate-limit-model-rpm: 900
x-rw-rate-limit-model-tpm: 18000
x-rw-rate-limit-model-concurrency: 8
x-rw-rate-limit-remaining: 0
x-request-id: rwd-req-0a1b2c3d
Content-Type: application/json
```
Curl repro they provided (sanitized):
```
curl -X POST https://api.redwood-inference.com/v1/chat -H "Authorization: Bearer <KEY>" -H "Content-Type: application/json" -d '{"model":"rwd-3-large","messages":[{"role":"system","content":"<64k context...>"},{"role":"user","content":"hi"}]}'
```
They say failures happen ~30% of requests during a 2 minute burst window.

Sophie Liu: OK — flagged as model-specific throttling. rwd-3-large has per-model RPM/TPM and a small max concurrency (8) in hosted tier. When you combine very long contexts (which increase tokens per request) and parallel workers, token throughput can blow past the model TPM and the per-second concurrency guard can drive 429s. TPM counts all tokens (prompt+completion). Bursts can exceed the token bucket refill rate and immediately hit x-rw-rate-limit-remaining == 0.

Raj Patel: Two notes from infra side:
1) The header shows model RPM=900 and TPM=18000 — that matches our catalog for rwd-3-large in hosted tier (non-dedicated).
2) Concurrency 8 means only 8 inflight requests for that model per account/region. Additional inflight requests get 429 with the model_concurrency code.

Ops Oncall: Also verify they aren't multiplexing a single API key across many workers without per-worker backoff. That pattern can produce steady-state 429s even at lower overall RPM because concurrency bursts coincide.

Emma Hart: Customer also sent a small repro that spams 16 parallel curl processes. They claim they used exponential backoff but still saw many 429s during the first 60 seconds.

Raj Patel: Expected. Short backoff windows + synchronous retries create thundering herd. Suggest change to one of: staggered jittered backoff, token-leaky bucket client-side, or reduce parallelism so in-flight <= model_concurrency.

Sophie Liu: Product guidance to share with customer:
- Reduce context length where possible (trim system/preamble for high-throughput paths).
- Use faster model variant (rwd-3-medium or a quantized variant) which has higher RPM/TPM and higher concurrency limits.
- If consistent high throughput is required, recommend Redwood Dedicated or private deployment — those can be provisioned with higher concurrency and reserved capacity.
- For bursty workloads, implement client-side queuing + exponential backoff with full-jitter.

Emma Hart: Billing Bot pulled usage spike for their API key: shows token usage jump to 62k tokens/min for a 3-minute window — explains why TPM limit tripped. Billing Bot: any billing flags?

Billing Bot: No invoice blocks. Their free trial credits were consumed earlier. This is purely throttling, not billing cut-off.

Ops Oncall: If customer needs immediate relief and is ok with a temporary mitigation, we can:
- Issue a short-lived higher concurrency override for their account (requires approval and risk ack), or
- Suggest they throttle clients to keep per-key concurrency <= 8 and tokens/min <= 18k.

Raj Patel: For reproduction we used a simple stress test locally: 
```
# spawn 16 parallel workers hitting same key
for i in {1..16}; do 
  while true; do 
    curl -s -X POST https://api.redwood-inference.com/v1/chat -H "Authorization: Bearer $KEY" -H "Content-Type: application/json" -d '{"model":"rwd-3-large","messages":[{"role":"user","content":"x"}] }' &
  done &
done
```
This reliably produced 429s and the response headers matched the ones above.

Emma Hart: Customer asked for concrete config example to avoid throttles — can we provide a snippet for node/python clients?

Sophie Liu: Sure, share this Node pseudo-example w/ jittered backoff and concurrency limit: 
```
const pLimit = require('p-limit');
const limit = pLimit(6); // keep under model concurrency 8
async function callWithBackoff(payload, retries=5) {
  let attempt = 0;
  while (attempt < retries) {
    try {
      return await fetch(...);
    } catch (err) {
      if (err.status === 429) {
        const jitter = Math.random() * 200;
        await sleep(2**attempt * 100 + jitter);
        attempt++;
        continue;
      }
      throw err;
    }
  }
  throw new Error('max retries');
}
// schedule tasks using limit(() => callWithBackoff(...))
```

Emma Hart: I'm going to respond to customer with: explanation of model limits (rpm/tpm/concurrency), attach repro findings, recommended mitigations (reduce context, lower parallelism, switch model, or upgrade to dedicated), and offer temporary override if they need immediate short-term relief. Any additions?

Raj Patel: Add note to include exact request logs (x-request-id) for each 429 so we can correlate in infra logs. Also request they timestamp their bursts and send sample request bodies so we can calculate tokens per request precisely.

Ops Oncall: I'll pre-approve a one-week concurrency bump for support-managed accounts but only after business signs the temporary SLA change. Otherwise recommend Dedicated.

Emma Hart: Great — filing follow-up to customer now. Ticket #INC-5421. Will include the node snippet and ask for x-request-ids. :thumbsup:
